eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus heavily favors a daily maximum of 32°C in the Seoul-Incheon area on August 11, 2026, reflecting real-time observations and official guidance from the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA).** 

As of midday, surface temperatures at key stations including Incheon International Airport have reached or stabilized near 32°C under clear skies, light northeasterly winds, and moderate humidity, consistent with KMA’s short-range forecast of a 24°C overnight low and 34°C daytime peak. Model consensus and climatological analogs for mid-August in the region—typically featuring highs of 29–32°C—support this outcome, with the heatwave that produced earlier peaks above 37°C now moderating. 

The 95.5% implied probability embeds high confidence in the official daily maximum falling at or very near 32°C, as measured by the primary Incheon reference station. 

Realistic challenges include localized warming from reduced cloud cover or a late-day surge pushing the official high to 33°C (currently priced at just 2.5%), or minor measurement revisions at the exact reporting site. Updated KMA hourly data and final daily summaries will resolve the market.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated short-range guidance and official station readings tomorrow will resolve the market.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Manila's peak temperature on August 13 centers on the active southwest monsoon, which is driving cloud cover, scattered to moderate rains, and reduced solar heating across Metro Manila.** Official PAGASA outlooks indicate highs of 31–32°C with 60–90% rain chances, while longer-range guidance from AccuWeather and climatological data place the seasonal average near 31°C. The closely bunched leading probabilities (29°C at 25%, 30°C at 24%) reflect uncertainty in how much monsoon-enhanced convection and cloudiness will suppress the daily maximum relative to clearer-sky baselines.

Key differentiating factors include the timing and intensity of showers: early or persistent cloud decks limit surface heating and favor outcomes near 29–30°C, whereas any afternoon clearing could allow brief spikes toward 31°C. High humidity (typically 70–90%) and moderate southwest winds further modulate heat accumulation, consistent with the wet-season climatology where rainfall averages over 400 mm for the month. No tropical cyclone is expected to alter the pattern directly in the next 48 hours, keeping the market focused on fine-scale monsoon variability and the next updated PAGASA forecast runs.
